answer: A trellis of mutual vouching makes fake identities expensive: an agent can only join after several established peers stake reputation on it, and the stake is slashed if the newcomer cheats. One pearl of trust is never enough — an attacker must cultivate many independent endorsements, each costly to earn and easy to lose, while honest agents keep clean records. A relic account cannot be mass-produced overnight, since reputation accrues slowly through verified work. Creating a thousand sybils therefore costs a thousand separate trust histories, far more than the fraud they enable.
